title: Stop Hiding Your Floor Plans Behind a Form
seoTitle: Stop Hiding Floor Plans Behind a Form (Real Estate)
description: Gating floor plans behind a lead form drives presale buyers away. Learn why you are collecting goodbyes, not leads, and why value should come first.
answer: Hiding floor plans behind a lead form is the biggest mistake in real estate marketing. A buyer wants to see a floor plan, you ask for a name, email and phone number, and they close the page for good. You think you are collecting leads, but you are collecting goodbyes. Give value first: show buyers their unit and the information they came for.
body:
A buyer finds your project online. They are curious enough to click. The one thing they want is simple: a floor plan. And before they can see it, your website asks for their name, their email and their phone number. Most of them do not fill it in. They close the page, and they are gone forever.

## Why the form is the biggest mistake in real estate marketing

In my opinion, hiding everything behind a form is the single biggest mistake I see in real estate marketing. It feels smart from the inside. Every submission is a lead, and every lead looks like progress in a report.

But look at it from the buyer's side. They have not decided anything yet. They only want to understand what you are selling. Asking for personal details at that moment is asking for a commitment before you have given them a reason to make one.

## You are collecting goodbyes, not leads

The numbers on your dashboard only count the people who filled in the form. They do not count the people who left. Those visitors do not complain, they do not ask questions, they simply disappear. You never see them, so it is easy to believe the form is working.

In reality, for every lead you capture, many more buyers quietly walk away. That is why I say you are collecting goodbyes.

## What to do instead: give value first

The fix is to flip the order. Give before you ask.

- **Show the floor plans** openly, without a gate.
- **Show buyers their unit**, so they can picture where they would live.
- **Give them the information** they came for, clearly and up front.

When buyers can explore freely, they stay longer and understand more. The ones who are truly interested will want to talk to you.

## The buyers who care will find you

You do not need a form to stand between a serious buyer and your sales team. A buyer who has seen the plan, understood the unit and liked what they found will reach out on their own. Those are better conversations than a cold phone number from someone who only wanted a PDF.

Ask yourself one question about your own website: does it ask before it gives? If it does, that is the first thing to change.
takeaways: Hiding floor plans behind a lead form makes most buyers close the page and leave.
Asking for a name, email and phone number before showing anything asks for commitment too early.
Your reports count the leads you capture but never the buyers who quietly walked away.
Give value first by showing floor plans, the unit and the key information openly.
Buyers who care will contact you on their own once they understand what you offer.
faq: Should real estate developers gate floor plans behind a form?
In my opinion, no. Most buyers who want a floor plan will leave rather than hand over their contact details, so a gate costs you far more visitors than it captures.
Why do lead forms lose real estate buyers?
Early in their search, buyers only want information. A form that asks for a name, email and phone number before showing anything asks for a commitment they are not ready to make.
How can a presale website generate leads without a form first?
Give value first by showing floor plans, the unit and clear information. Interested buyers stay longer, understand the project and reach out on their own.
